title: Run through a serialized literal
statement: Let $x$ be a bit string, $B,v\in\mathbb{N}$, $s,b\in\{0,1\}$, and let $st=(K,S,P,T,Z,C,V)$ be a seven-register state. Suppose the suffix of $x$ starting at position $P$ is the serialization $1^{v+1}0b$ followed by a bit string $rest$, every register of $st$ is at most $B$, and $|x|\leq B$. If the scratch registers $T,Z,C,V$ are zero, the machine has a guarded run from label $lt(s)$ with state $st$ to label $cl(s\lor(\mathrm{asg}(K,S,v)=b))$ with state $(K,S,P+v+3,T,Z,C,V)$.
hypotheses_covered: the input suffix at position $P$ is the encoding of $(v,b)$ followed by $rest$
all seven registers are at most $B$
the input length is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $s,b$ bits, $v$ a natural number, $rest$
a bit string, and $st$ a seven-register state. Suppose the suffix of $x$ beginning at
position $st.P$ is the serialization of the literal $(v,b)$ followed by $rest$, every
register of $st$ is at most $B$, $|x|\leq B$, and the scratch registers $T,Z,C,V$ are
zero. Then the machine has a guarded run from state $\mathrm{lt}(s)$ and register state
$st$ to state $\mathrm{cl}(s\lor(\mathrm{asg}(st.K,st.S,v)=b))$ with the same registers
except that $P$ is increased by $v+3$.
